text: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt—those settled in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the region of Pathros:

This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You yourselves saw all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Look at them today—ruins, with no one living in them,
because of the evil they did to provoke me, going off to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor you nor your fathers had ever known.
Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets, saying, "Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!"
But they would not listen or pay attention; they would not turn from their evil or stop burning incense to other gods.
So my fury and my anger poured out and blazed through the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they became the desolate ruins they are today.

And now, this is what the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves, cutting off from Judah man and woman, child and infant, leaving yourselves no remnant at all?

Why provoke me with what your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live? You will destroy yourselves and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of the kings of Judah and their wives, and your own evils and the evils of your wives, committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have shown no remorse, no fear; they have not walked in my law and my statutes, which I set before you and before your fathers.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am setting my face against you for disaster, to cut off all Judah.

I will take the remnant of Judah who were determined to go to the land of Egypt and settle there, and they will all meet their end in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and be consumed by famine; from the least to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine, and they will become an object of cursing and horror, of scorn and reproach.
I will punish those living in the land of Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem—with the sword, with famine, and with plague.

None of the remnant of Judah who have gone to live in the land of Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, though they long to return and live there. Not one will return, except a few fugitives.

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, along with all the women standing there—a great assembly—and all the people living in the land of Egypt, in the region of Pathros, answered Jeremiah:

versions.text: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, along with all the women standing there—a great assembly—and all the people living in Lower and Upper Egypt, answered Jeremiah:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "in the land of Egypt, in Pathros." Rendering it as "Lower and Upper Egypt" is an interpretation that also creates an inconsistency with verse 1, where Pathros is retained as a place name. Keeping the place name preserves the geographic link between the opening address and the people's reply.

text: "As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD—we will not listen to you.

We will most certainly do everything we said we would: we will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we did—we and our fathers, our kings and our officials—in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food, we prospered, and we saw no disaster.

versions.text: We will most certainly do everything we have vowed: we will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we did—we and our fathers, our kings and our officials—in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food, we prospered, and we saw no disaster.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew here is "everything that has gone out of our mouth," i.e., what they have declared; the explicit vocabulary of vows (נדר) only enters at verse 25. Using "said we would" keeps the distinction between their declaration here and the vows named later.

text: But ever since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine."

And the women added, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands' knowledge that we made cakes shaped in her image and poured out drink offerings to her?"
Then Jeremiah said to all the people—the men and the women, all who had answered him:

"The incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your officials and the people of the land—did the LORD not remember it? Did it not rise up in his mind?
When the LORD could no longer bear the evil of your deeds and the detestable things you did, your land became a desolate ruin and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.

Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD or walk in his law, his statutes, and his decrees, this disaster has overtaken you, as it has today."
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women: "Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have said with your mouths and carried out with your hands, 'We will certainly fulfill the vows we made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Very well—keep your vows! Carry them out!

Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah living in the land of Egypt: I swear by my great name, says the LORD, that never again will my name be invoked by anyone of Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt, saying, 'As the Lord GOD lives.'

versions.text: But hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah living in Egypt: I swear by my great name, says the LORD, that never again will my name be invoked by anyone of Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt, saying, 'As the Lord GOD lives.'
versions.explanation: Hebrew לָכֵן is a consequential connective ('therefore'), drawing the conclusion from the preceding oracle, not an adversative ('but'). The change also restores 'the land of Egypt' matching בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם.

text: See, I am watching over them for harm, not for good. Every man of Judah in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are finished.

versions.text: I am watching over them for harm, not for good. Every man of Judah in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are finished.
versions.explanation: The emphatic particle הִנְנִי is left untranslated here, though it is rendered elsewhere in the chapter ('I am going to...'). A brief 'See,' preserves the emphasis and gives the line a stronger oral opening.

text: Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, only a few in number. Then the whole remnant of Judah who came to live in Egypt will know whose word stands—mine or theirs.
This will be the sign to you, declares the LORD, that I am going to punish you in this place, so you may know that my words against you will surely stand, bringing disaster:

This is what the LORD says: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.

versions.text: This is what the LORD says: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, who sought his life."
versions.explanation: The closing quotation mark has no matching opening mark anywhere in the section, so it should be removed for consistency. Also, removing the comma before 'who sought his life' makes the clause restrictive, matching the Hebrew apposition אֹיְבוֹ וּמְבַקֵּשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ.
